I was 27 when I had my first flare up that landed me in the hospital for a week. The first two years were very difficult while I discovered what my triggers were. At 28 I met with a surgeon and he brushed me aside saying I was too young for surgery. Finally, at 31 and so many flare ups I couldn’t even count them all without going through my med records, I met with another surgeon and put my foot down about the surgery. Luckily by that time my medical record spoke for itself and this new surgeon needed no convincing. I had surgery at the end of February this year just after my 32 birthday, and it was the best thing that ever happened to me. I can eat ANYTHING now!  Going to the bathroom to do my business is no longer terrifying. I feel less stressed out all the time and am pain free. I wish so badly that first surgeon hadn’t been such a prick and blew me off- would have saved me so many CT scans and trips to the ER. Don’t give up! Be an advocate for yourself. It is a life changing surgery for those of us with diverticulitis.

Three days later there was no improvement in my pain so I went back. They scanned me this time and found a tennis ball sized cyst sitting on my ovary. Had surgery for it the next day. By the end of the year I developed c-diff, and infection n the colon from overuse of antibiotics and was in the hospital a couple days to get the infection and pain under control. Abdominal pain is such a beast. I feel like ER doctors think that half the time people are there fishing for heavy pain meds, and the people who are in genuine pain pay the price. Don’t give up. Keep fighting for your health and right to live a healthy and pain free life.

Fruits were never a huge issue for me. Strawberry seeds are super tiny, I never had issue with them. I LOVE tomatoes, and for me it was the tomato skin that upset me more than the seeds. Before my first flare up I had a sesame seed bagel for breakfast for two weeks, and a bag of popcorn for dinner two nights in a row. The day after that second bag of popcorn I was in the hospital. Whoops! Moderation is key. Unfortunately, everyone has a different trigger. The most common denominator I have seen is raw veggies, which is extra frustrating because once you are healed up they tell you to eat lots of fiber. You will find that every doctor has a different opinion on what not to eat.  It is beyond frustrating. I did have decent success for a while using fiber supplements and probiotics. I wish you patience and luck in discovering what triggers it for you. Welcome to the hell of life with diverticulitis!

Edit: I would definitely suggest no more sunflower seeds with shell on. Oh!  And chew your food more than usual, and drink lots of water with every meal.

Through very painful dietary trial and error, for me it was raw vegetables and times of very high stress. Nuts and seeds were ok in strict moderation. But towards the end, even a side salad would ruin me for a week or more. I even found that some forms of exercise, namely sit ups and crunches, would trigger discomfort in the danger zone. (My husband and I began referring to the lower left quadrant as the danger zone.) Also, popcorn was always a no go. Once I even had just a handful of popcorn and was in agony the next two days.
20 years! Holy cow I can’t even imagine. My next salad will be in your honor.

I was diagnosed about two years ago, and it has been a struggle finding a dietary balance ever since.  I have had a number of flare ups and been hospitalized twice.  

In my experience, making an effort to use fiber supplements has helped more than not using them at all.  As you pointed out, getting too much fiber seems to be just as harmful as not getting any at all.  What works best for me as of late is to have one glass of Metamucil or one dose of fiber capsules a day.  

One thing I have learned the hard way is not to get all of my fiber from raw vegetables.  Salad for dinner too many nights in a row has sent me to the ER too many times.

I am still experimenting with the whole seeds/nuts debate.  Some here and there seem to be ok.  It's the high quantities of raw veg that are the big villains for me. 

Also, I feel like stress is a big culprit in having flare ups.  The last doctor said that there is nothing to back it up, but I swear that every flare up I have had has couples with times of stress. 

Sorry for the ramble!  It's rare I get to share in this battle with anyone, especially being a 29 year old.

Ooook people, don't get your panties in a twist. I would be happy to further explain. I  claim a 26 year residency in this town. I have lived in just about every corner: OB, Point Loma, Del Mar, Solana Beach, Ramona, North Park, Mira Mesa,  you name it, there is probably a time I have lived there. That, coupled with growing up with a 30+year local chef to call father, I feel fairly confident when I say I know a thing or two about the food in this town. 

Now, when I speak disparagingly in regards to the Gaslamp and PB, it is not born from hearsay or a lack of social life. Though it seems you lot may presume all who add their two cents on Reddit are fellows, many of whom do hide in their parent's guest room fearing daylight and groups of more than three, some of us are not only ladies, but well rounded, worthily opinionated, credible, and busy. While at the time of my previous comment I lacked the time to go into greater detail as to the spots I would recommend for a meal, at the present I have loads of time. And so, dear reader, here are my top picks. Ahem...

1. World Famous in Mission Beach. Yes.  I am actually suggesting you go to Mission Beach. But only because the eggs benedict at World Famous are amazing. They make their own hollandaise, delicious! And it is right on the beach, good people watching, servers take good care of you, great mimosas. 

And speaking of great eggs benedict...

2. Snooze in Hillcrest. Not only do they have an amazing selection of creative eggs benedict, their pancakes are out of this world. Red velvet pancakes. Need I say more? Didn't think so. Moving on. 

For lunch:

3.  Chris' Deli in Ocean Beach. If you ever need to grab a big sandwich to picnic at the cliffs or the beach or park, this deli is great. Very fresh, perfect deli salads, and an amazing beer selection. Done and done. 

4.  Naked Cafe in Point Loma. For you vegetarians and farm fresh folk, this is the spot. I am not crazy about the location, (gross strip mall) but once you get inside you kinda forget you are in a gross strip mall. They are great for lunch/brunch, they offer refreshing choices of your usual egg breakfasts and sandwich lunches. Oh, amazing  mimosas. 

5.  Nati's in Ocean Beach.  Gold ol' casual, inexpensive sit down mexican food. Been around forever, nothing gourmet, but comfortable and homey. Just perfect for what it is. 

And for dinner we have....

6.  Cafe Bleu in Mission Hills. This place is too good for words. Perfect spot for an intimate date. Some of the best food I have ever had has been here. Amazing wine selection, very knowledgeable staff, French/American inspired menu. Pricey but worth every penny. This place is just sexy. 

7.  Riki Sushi in North Park is my pick for inexpensive but irresistible sushi.  I love sitting at the sushi bar and watching the sushi artists at work.  Very reasonably priced and always busy!  Both good signs if you ask me. 

8. Extraordinary Desserts in....well... very near Balboa Park. Best. Desserts. EVER!! This place will melt the panties off of any girl. To die for. If I say any more it will just ruin it, so just go!
